findings.title: Imported feed/remote HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method raw_html, and Post#cook returns raw unchanged for such posts. Neither import nor absolutize_urls strips script tags, event-handler attributes, javascript: URLs, or other dangerous markup, and PollFeed passes RSS/Atom content directly into import. A malicious or compromised feed item can therefore store arbitrary HTML/JavaScript as post.cooked, which is rendered raw in Discourse and in embed views, giving stored XSS in forum visitors' browsers.

findings.title: PollFeed crashes on feed items without a content element
findings.body: poll_feed unconditionally calls i.content.scrub for every item. Ordinary RSS items commonly have description instead of content (and Atom/RSS variants expose different fields), so i.content can be nil and this raises NoMethodError. Because the exception is inside rss.items.each with sidekiq retry disabled, one such item aborts the whole hourly poll and prevents all remaining items from being imported.

findings.title: Concurrent imports for the same URL race the unique embed_url index
findings.body: import does a non-atomic check-then-create: it looks up TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first and only creates the embed after PostCreator runs. Two concurrent RetrieveTopic/PollFeed executions for the same new URL can both see no embed, both create topics/posts, and then the second TopicEmbed.create! raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique from the unique index instead of returning the already-created post, failing the job after doing duplicate creation work. The lookup/create needs an atomic rescue/retry or locking strategy.

findings.title: Embed controller spec expects synchronous TopicRetriever but controller enqueues a job
findings.body: The 'tells the topic retriever to work' example stubs TopicRetriever.new/retrieve, but EmbedController#best never instantiates TopicRetriever; it calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...). The mock expectation will not be satisfied and this spec fails, leaving the actual enqueue arguments (user_id and embed_url) untested. The spec should expect Jobs.enqueue with :retrieve_topic instead.

findings.title: Disqus import drops the category option and now depends on fetching the live source site
findings.body: The import task removed the --category option and replaced local topic creation (with the thread's title, permalink body, created_at, and chosen category) with TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...), which performs open(url).read on each Disqus thread link. Existing invocations using -c will no longer place topics in the requested category, threads whose original site is offline, moved, or blocks fetching will fail the import, and the thread's original creation date is no longer used for the imported topic.

findings.title: absolutize_urls only fixes root-relative URLs, leaving other relative links broken
findings.body: absolutize_urls only rewrites href/src values that start with '/'. Feed and readability content frequently uses document-relative URLs such as href="page2.html" or src="images/pic.jpg" and protocol-relative URLs such as src="//cdn.example.com/x.jpg"; those are left untouched, so after import they resolve against the Discourse host instead of the source site and produce wrong links or 404 images in the imported post.

findings.title: import_remote fetches arbitrary URLs server-side with no timeout or size limit
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import_remote does open(url).read with no timeout, redirect restriction, or response-size cap before Readability parsing. Via EmbedController/RetrieveTopic the URL is user-influenced (constrained only by host equality at the retriever layer), so requests can make the server fetch large or slow resources on the embeddable host, exhausting job workers/memory; the fetched result is then published as a topic, which can also disclose content the server can reach but an anonymous visitor could not. Add timeouts, size limits, and scheme/host validation inside import_remote itself.
